text:
incident-bot: ALERT — Canary error-rate spike detected for model variant redwood-v2-canary in us-west-2. 5m error rate = 18% (threshold 5%). Smart routing fallback activated; seeing a high rate of sticky affinity rebinds. Paging on-call @maya-oncall :rotating_light:

maya-oncall: I’m on it, reading logs now. Can someone confirm whether rollout policy is still in 'gradual' state?

sre-jen: Canary is at 12% traffic. Policy shows canary -> stable fallback enabled with sticky_affinity=ON. Looks like failed reqs from canary are triggering fallback, but session affinity cookie TTL not clearing so some sessions bounce back to canary after health check. That creates a soft oscillation.

infra-han: grep of router logs shows repeated route decision entries:
```
route_decision: user=acct_42 variant=redwood-v2-canary -> fallback=redwood-stable reason=instance_unhealthy
route_decision: user=acct_42 affinity=sticky variant=redwood-v2-canary ttl=0 -> route back to canary
```
We have many of those for same session IDs, roughly every 3s.

product-lee: Customers: 3 enterprise customers in us-west have reported increased 500s and elevated latencies on chat endpoints. Impact appears intermittent (sessions can recover) but enough to trigger a first-response SLA page.

ops-nima: Suggested immediate mitigations (in order):
1) Pause the canary rollout (so no new sticky binds to canary).
2) Evict sticky affinity keys for affected region to force fresh routing decisions.
3) Increase fallback cooldown on smart router to avoid immediate rebinds.
4) If above fails, rollback canary to previous stable image.

maya-oncall: I'm going to pause the rollout now. Taking action: pause via control-plane API.

deploy-bot: API: POST /v1/rollouts/pause { "rollout_id":"canary/rd-124","actor":"maya-oncall" } -> 202 Accepted. rollout_state=PAUSED

sre-jen: Good. Next I will run affinity eviction for us-west-2 for keys with high oscillation. Command I’ll run:
```bash
rgc affinity evict --region us-west-2 --selector "variant=redwood-v2-canary AND oscillation>3m"
```
Expect it to take ~30s to propagate.

infra-han: Before you evict, note that eviction triggers short bursts while sessions re-resolve — recommend setting fallback_cooldown to 30s to avoid immediate rebind. I’ll apply that change.

infra-han: Applying policy change:
```json
PATCH /v1/policies/smart-routing/rd-124
{ "fallback_cooldown_seconds": 30 }
```
apply -> 200 OK.

sre-jen: Eviction started. Monitoring logs for user acct_42.

(30s later)

sre-jen: Eviction completed. Router logs show session IDs re-resolving to redwood-stable; error-rate for canary in us-west-2 dropped to 6% over 5m, overall platform 5xxs down 60%.

product-lee: Do we have customer-facing note? I’ll draft a short note for impacted customers: describe transient errors, mitigation, and that we paused the canary and will follow up with RCA.

maya-oncall: I’ll own the post-incident follow-up and coordinate the RCA. Assigning follow-ups:
- SRE (jen): collect trace samples + correlation of affinity TTLs and healthcheck failures.
- Infra (han): audit affinity implementation for TTL=0 edge-case and add guardrails.
- Product (lee): customer comms draft and impacted tenant list.

ops-nima: We should also add an automated check to detect 'affinity oscillation' patterns: repeated route decisions for same session within short window. Flagging as new monitoring ticket.

deploy-bot: Rollout pause still in effect. If you want to rollback, use:
```bash
rgc rollout rollback --id canary/rd-124 --to-version redwood-v1-stable
```

sre-jen: For now we’ll monitor for 15m before rollback. If error-rate median > 7% in region after coolant expires, escalate to rollback.

maya-oncall: Noting customer impact: minor-visible outages for 3 customers, intermittent errors for others. SLA page triggered but no full outage.

product-lee: I’ll send the initial customer note in 10m once we confirm stabilized metrics.

(15m later)

sre-jen: Metrics look stable: region error-rate 3.2%, global 1.1%. No further oscillation traces. Cancelling rollback for now.

maya-oncall: Closing the P0 page. Opening postmortem ticket and scheduling RCA with SRE+Infra+Product. ACTIONS:
- (sre-jen) collect sample traces + prepare mitigation runbook for affinity eviction -> due EOD
- (infra-han) patch affinity TTL handling and add unit tests -> PR by EOD+1
- (ops-nima) add monitoring rule for affinity oscillation -> ticket created #INC-7931
- (product-lee) customer comms sent and follow-up plan -> sent

sre-jen: Notes for RCA: primary root cause appears to be an edge case in affinity TTL where TTL=0 cookies still considered sticky by router after fallback. When fallback happened, router re-wrote cookie but left TTL unset, so subsequent requests were evaluated as sticky to canary. That created mini-loops on health checks.

maya-oncall: Thanks everyone. Tagging follow-ups in the postmortem. If anything re-surfaces ping this thread. :thumbsup:
